contracts.commit_point: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail='no user') terminating request processing prior to any agent orchestration or Cosmos DB effect — representative site app_kernel.py:112; identical commit sites at app_kernel.py:253, :360, :473, :873.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Per-endpoint inline identity guard: get_authenticated_user_details(request.headers) extracts x-ms-client-principal-id from EasyAuth headers (auth_utils.py:6-32); each endpoint then checks `if not user_id:` and raises HTTPException(status_code=400, detail='no user') before any orchestration or store call (app_kernel.py:105-112, 247-253, 354-360, 467-473, 867-873).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A request lacking an authenticated user principal id (falsy user_principal_id derived from x-ms-client-principal-id) proceeds past the endpoint identity guard — i.e., the mutating endpoint fails to terminate processing with HTTPException 400 ('no user') before any downstream effect.
pending_binding_information: Content of src/backend/auth/sample_user (sample_user.sample_user) is needed to determine whether the fallback supplies a non-empty x-ms-client-principal-id, which decides whether the HTTP 400 rejection is reachable when the EasyAuth header is absent.

No supplied source binds this HTTP guard to an agent tool registration, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input; if such a binding exists (e.g., in AgentFactory or agent handler sources, not supplied), agent_mediation should be revised from not_established and an agent_entry_binding evidence entry added.
contracts.protected_operation: Request handling of the five mutating API endpoints that trigger plan creation, human feedback/clarification, step approval, or bulk message deletion.
contracts.protected_resource: Backend mutating request-processing pipelines of the multi-agent planning service (pre-effect request admission).
contracts.protection_obligation: Mutating backend endpoints (POST /api/input_task, POST /api/human_feedback, POST human_clarification, POST /api/approve_step_or_steps, DELETE /api/messages) must reject with HTTP 400 any request lacking an authenticated user principal id, before executing any downstream plan-creation, feedback/approval, or message-deletion effect. (Merged from both reviewer obligations: duplicate wording of the same identity-rejection duty.)
scope_limits: Compiled only for the five mutating endpoints cited; the identical guard also appears on read-only GET endpoints, which are out of scope for this contract (see missing_information).

Guard strength depends on the dev-mode fallback in auth_utils.py:10-15: a missing x-ms-client-principal-id header is replaced by sample_user.sample_user (module content not supplied), so whether the 400 branch can ever fire without the header is unresolved.
Principal id is taken from request headers as-is; no cryptographic verification is present in the supplied source (hosting-layer EasyAuth enforcement is not shown).
CORS middleware (app_kernel.py:71-77) and health-check middleware (app_kernel.py:80) are outside this contract.
The RAI content gate at app_kernel.py:90-104 is a distinct mechanism, not part of this identity obligation.

contracts.declared_mechanism: Endpoint identity guard raising HTTP 400 when user_id is falsy (app_kernel.py:867-873), followed by CosmosMemoryContext.delete_all_items → delete_all_messages, whose query is restricted by 'WHERE c.data_type=@data_type AND c.user_id=@user_id' (cosmos_memory_kernel.py:490-497) and executes per-item delete_item via delete_items_by_query (cosmos_memory_kernel.py:474-488).

contracts.protected_operation: DELETE /api/messages handling: the four delete_all_items calls for data types plan, session, step, and agent_message (app_kernel.py:878-881).
contracts.protected_resource: Cosmos DB container documents of data_type 'plan', 'session', 'step', and 'agent_message' belonging to the authenticated user.
contracts.protection_obligation: DELETE /api/messages must execute its bulk Cosmos DB deletion of plan/session/step/agent_message items only after the endpoint identity guard passes, and the deletion must remain scoped to the authenticated user_id (destructive operations scoped to user_id per reviewer obligation two).
scope_limits: delete_item failures inside delete_items_by_query are caught and logged, not re-raised (cosmos_memory_kernel.py:487-488), so partial deletion can occur silently; the guard does not make deletion transactional.
AgentFactory.clear_cache() at app_kernel.py:884 is an in-process state mutation outside the database stratum and is not covered by this contract.
Deletion is cross-session for the authenticated user (no session_id parameter); scoping relies solely on the stored user_id field value of each document.
